title: Summarizing an array
summary: Largest so far, totals, and stopping early.

say.never: To find the biggest number: start by assuming the first one is the biggest. Then look at each of the others in turn, and whenever you find a bigger one, swap it in. When you've looked at them all, `best` holds the winner.
say.bit: Start with the first value, then replace it whenever you find a bigger one.

steps.title: Stop as soon as you know

say.never: When you're searching for something, you can stop the moment you find it: `return true` right away. Only after checking *every* box without a match do you return `false`. That's why the `return false` is after the loop.
say.bit: Return true as soon as one item matches; return false only after checking them all.

say.never: An average is the total divided by how many there are. Careful: if both are whole numbers, Java throws away the decimals. Writing `(double) sum` first turns the total into a decimal number, so the answer keeps its decimals.
say.bit: Average is total divided by count. Cast to `double` first so integer division doesn't drop the decimals.
